description: Type exact CPT/ICD-10 codes like the CCA exam. Decimals and laterality required.

questions.explanation: G90.522 — Disorders of the autonomic nervous system, causalgia of lower limb. The 5th/6th characters specify laterality and limb.
questions.hint: G90.5 category — needs 6 characters with decimal.
questions.q: Type the ICD-10-CM code for: Reflex sympathetic dystrophy of the lower limb

questions.explanation: 64520 is the injection code; -LT specifies left side. Laterality modifiers are required — without it the claim denies.
questions.q: Type the CPT code (with laterality modifier) for: Paravertebral sympathetic nerve injection, left side, single level

questions.explanation: 77003 — fluoroscopic guidance for needle placement is separately reportable with 64520 per CPT Assistant.
questions.q: Type the CPT code for: Fluoroscopic guidance for needle placement (e.g., with 64520)

questions.explanation: 99213 — office/outpatient visit, established patient, low MDM. The most common E/M code in billing.
questions.q: Type the CPT code for: Established patient office visit, low complexity (the workhorse E/M)

questions.explanation: 11102 — tangential biopsy of skin, single lesion. (11100 was deleted; 11102/11103 replaced it.)
questions.q: Type the CPT code for: Skin biopsy, single lesion (tangential/shave)

questions.explanation: 36415 — collection of venous blood by venipuncture. Bundled into E/M under NCCI unless separately identifiable.
questions.q: Type the CPT code for: Venipuncture — routine blood draw

questions.explanation: 20610 — arthrocentesis, aspiration and/or injection of a major joint (knee, shoulder, hip).
questions.q: Type the CPT code for: Major joint injection — knee arthrocentesis with steroid

questions.explanation: J1956 — levofloxacin injection, 250 mg. 500 mg administered = 2 units on the claim line.
questions.q: Type the HCPCS code for: Levofloxacin injection, per 250 mg (physician gave 500 mg)

questions.explanation: 99213-95 — the -95 modifier flags synchronous telehealth. POS 02 is also required on the claim.
questions.q: Type the CPT code (with modifier) for: Telehealth office visit, established patient, low complexity

questions.explanation: E11.42 — Type 2 diabetes with diabetic polyneuropathy. Combination code; do not code neuropathy separately.
questions.q: Type the ICD-10-CM code for: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic neuropathy

title: Code Entry Drills

description: Read real EOB/ERA lines. Calculate adjustments, patient responsibility, and next steps.

questions.explanation: Contractual adjustment = Billed − Allowed = $150 − $100 = $50 (CO-45). The $20 copay (PR-3) is patient responsibility; the payer paid $80.
questions.hint: CO-45 is always Billed minus Allowed.
questions.q: Review the EOB line below. What is the contractual adjustment?

questions.explanation: Patient owes the $20 copay (PR-3). The $50 (CO-45) is a contractual write-off — never bill the patient for CO amounts.
questions.hint: PR = patient responsibility. Which PR code is shown?
questions.q: Review the EOB line below. How much does the patient owe?

questions.explanation: CO-50 (medical necessity) is NOT a routine contractual adjustment. The $60 shortfall needs review — it may be appealable with documentation. Writing it off blindly loses revenue.
questions.hint: CO-50 is never an automatic write-off.
options: Write off the $60 difference as contractual
Bill the patient for the $60 balance
Flag as possible underpayment / medical-necessity denial — review before writing off
questions.q: Review the ERA line below. What is the correct next step?

questions.explanation: CO-97 + M15 = bundled into another service (the E/M). The $25 is absorbed — do not bill the patient. Only appeal if a valid modifier (e.g., -59) was warranted.
options: The claim was denied for timely filing
The venipuncture was bundled into the E/M — $0 is correct, do not bill the patient
The payer made an error — appeal immediately
questions.q: Review the EOB line below. What happened here?

questions.explanation: $28 ÷ $140 allowed = 20% coinsurance (PR-2). The payer paid 80% ($112). Math always runs on the ALLOWED amount, not billed.
questions.q: Review the ERA line below. What is the coinsurance percentage?

questions.explanation: Only the $20 copay (PR-3) is patient responsibility. The bundled 36415 (CO-97, $0 allowed) is absorbed by the provider. Total patient owes: $20.
questions.hint: CO amounts are never patient responsibility.
questions.q: Review the two EOB lines below. What is the total patient responsibility?

questions.explanation: Paid = Allowed ($160) with no PR codes means the payer covered everything. $40 ($200−$160) is the contractual write-off. Zero patient balance — close the account.
questions.hint: No PR codes = no patient share.
options: The patient still owes a copay
Paid in full — $40 contractual adjustment, zero patient balance
questions.q: Review the ERA line below. What does this tell you?

questions.explanation: J1956 = 250 mg per unit. 500 mg ÷ 250 = 2 units. Correct. (And PR-2 $18 = 20% of $90 allowed — the math checks out.)
options: Yes — 2 units is correct for 500 mg
questions.q: Review the EOB line below. Is the unit count correct?

title: EOB Math Drills

description: A denied line hits your queue. Pick the correct NEXT ACTION — like a real biller.

questions.explanation: CO-29 with no proof of timely filing = write-off. Appeals without proof are rarely overturned. Calendar payer limits to prevent this.
questions.q: A denied line hits your queue (see panel). DOS was 14 months ago, payer is Aetna commercial (120-day limit). No proof of timely filing exists. What is the correct NEXT ACTION?

denial.reason: Time limit for filing has expired

questions.explanation: CO-16 + N286 is a fixable data error — add the referring NPI and send a CORRECTED claim. Never appeal a data error; appeals are for medical-necessity disputes.
questions.q: A denied line hits your queue (see panel). The referral was on file but the NPI was left off the claim. What is the correct NEXT ACTION?

questions.explanation: Routine venipuncture bundled into the E/M with no distinct-service justification = legitimate bundling. Write it off; do not bill the patient for CO-97.
questions.hint: Was the draw separately identifiable? No.
questions.q: A denied line hits your queue (see panel). The blood draw was a routine part of the visit. What is the correct NEXT ACTION?

questions.explanation: CO-18 with the original still processing = do NOT resubmit. Resubmitting creates another duplicate. Wait for the original to adjudicate, then work the outcome.
questions.hint: Original still processing — what happens if you resubmit?
questions.q: A denied line hits your queue (see panel). You check and the original claim from last month is still in 'processing' status. What is the correct NEXT ACTION?

questions.explanation: CO-197 — obtain the retro authorization NOW (within the 30-day window), then appeal with the auth number. Speed matters; after 30 days this becomes a write-off.
questions.hint: Retro auth window is still open.
questions.q: A denied line hits your queue (see panel). The surgery was elective, no auth was obtained. The payer allows retro auth within 30 days; DOS was 10 days ago. What is the correct NEXT ACTION?

questions.explanation: MA130 = unprocessable, NOT a denial. It was never adjudicated, so there is nothing to appeal or correct — submit a brand NEW claim with the DOB included.
questions.hint: MA130 is not appealable — what does that leave?
questions.q: A rejected line hits your queue (see panel). The claim is missing the patient's date of birth entirely. What is the correct NEXT ACTION?

questions.explanation: CO-22 = COB order error. Bill the PRIMARY (BCBS employer plan) first with a corrected claim, then send the balance to Medicare secondary. Wrong order always denies.
questions.hint: Which payer is primary for a working-aged patient?
questions.q: A denied line hits your queue (see panel). Patient has BCBS primary through employer and Medicare. You billed Medicare first. What is the correct NEXT ACTION?

denial.reason: May be covered by another payer

questions.explanation: CO-50 with documentation that genuinely does not support medical necessity = write-off. An appeal without supporting documentation will fail and waste the appeal window.
questions.hint: Does the documentation support the service? No.
questions.q: A denied line hits your queue (see panel). The sleep study was ordered for simple snoring with no documented apnea symptoms. What is the correct NEXT ACTION?

questions.explanation: CO-11 here is a coding error — the lesion diagnosis (e.g., D48.5) was in the note but Z00.00 was coded. Fix the diagnosis and send a corrected claim.
questions.hint: The right diagnosis is in the note — what kind of fix is that?
questions.q: A denied line hits your queue (see panel). The claim billed Z00.00 but the note documents a suspicious lesion that was biopsied. What is the correct NEXT ACTION?

questions.explanation: CO-4 = modifier error. -25 belongs ONLY on the E/M (99213), never on a procedure. Move the modifier and send a corrected claim.
questions.q: A denied line hits your queue (see panel). The documentation supports both the E/M and the injection. What is the correct NEXT ACTION?
